title: Latency-aware traffic fence for safe batching/caching config rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an automated pipeline that proposes batching and KV-cache configuration suggestions and applies them safely to serving clusters using a latency-first "traffic fence" layer. The traffic fence enforces per-route and per-customer SLOs (p99 latency, p50/p95 throughput) while allowing controlled cost-saving ramps. This ticket covers the design and initial implementation of the fence, the anomaly detector integrated with our metrics stream, and a staged apply/rollback mechanism that can perform quick rollback on observed regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Automated recommendations endpoint returns stable candidate config sets with expected token-cost reduction and predicted latency delta for a given route
Traffic fence can 'quarantine' a rollout and route X% of traffic to a candidate config while keeping the remainder on baseline
Anomaly detector flags regressions within 3 minutes of a p99 latency threshold breach and triggers rollback policy
Playbook documented: how to interpret recommendation scoring, start a staged rollout, and execute emergency rollback
Integration tests that simulate increased load and validate that the fence prevents p99 SLO violations across 3 synthetic workloads
success_metrics: Median token cost per request reduced by >= 8% for pilot routes without SLO breaches
Number of manual interventions for rollout failures reduced by 60% over current manual tuning
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Recommendation infra + dry-run scoring (internal routes only). Phase 2: Canary apply via traffic fence at 1–5% with tight SLO gates. Phase 3: Gradual ramp (5% -> 25% -> 50%) with automated verification windows and automated rollback on threshold breach. Phase 4: Full apply with continuous monitoring and periodic re-evaluation. All phases include a manual abort button and runbook references.
monitoring: Dashboards: per-route latency distribution, token-cost delta, throughput, error rate
Alert: p99 latency > configured SLO for 3 consecutive minutes -> severity P0 alert and fence quarantine
Alert: throughput drop > 20% correlated with candidate config -> notify SRE and quarantine
Audit log: every automated apply/rollback entry stored with config diff and metric snapshot
tasks: Design recommendation scoring model and features (latency sensitivity, request size histogram, cache hit potential)
Implement recommendations API and store candidate profiles
Build traffic fence middleware that supports percentage-based routing and quarantine semantics
Wire anomaly detector to metrics stream (Prometheus -> pipeline -> detector) and define thresholds
Create canary control-plane endpoints to apply candidate configs with tags and audit entries
Implement automatic rollback actuator and safe backoff strategy
Add end-to-end integration tests and chaos scenarios for false positives/negatives
Document runbook and add Console UX hooks for manual override
comments: 2026-02-28 - Aisha Patel: Kicked off scoping — initial design doc in drive (link below). Decided to prioritize latency-first gate over pure cost delta; rationale: production outages from aggressive batching are high impact.

2026-03-03 - Marcus Nguyen: Spike complete for a lightweight traffic fence prototype that rewrites routing rules at the proxy layer. Prototype can split traffic by percentage and attach tag metadata for metrics correlation.
2026-03-05 - Design review (Eli Torres): suggested making the fence per-customer as well as per-route. Added label for multitenancy considerations.

2026-03-07 - SRE feedback (Priya Rao): require an explicit 'kill switch' in the control plane and an audit trail for regulatory customers. Also recommended a longer verification window for enterprise customers (10m vs. 3m).

2026-03-10 - Marcus Nguyen: Implemented detector integration (initial version) — uses moving-window p99 with baseline drift correction. Early tests show detection within ~2.5 minutes on synthetic bursts.
2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel: Paired with ML team to add a confidence score on recommendations — score used to determine maximum initial canary percentage. Added to follow-ups.
